solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Robust compilers are going to do our job

blocks.note: a crossword compiler's job is to set puzzles

explanation.surface: The setters boast that they are about to get down to work.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as a sentence the setters say about themselves: we'll set.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-set person has a solid, sturdy build, which is what robust describes.

clue.text: 1980s band welcoming a day in Oxford college

explanation.surface: A pop group from the eighties spends a day playing at an Oxford college.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted pair lands right after the band's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wadham, founded in 1610, is one of the constituent colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: Small, fast runner always obstructed by obstacle

blocks.note: a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A quick little runner keeps being tripped up by a hurdle.
explanation.walkthrough: The old sense of let as an obstruction survives in tennis and in legal phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a young hare: small because it is a baby, fast because hares are.

clue.text: Location of websites grasped by visionary poet

indicators.note: the seer holds the phrase inside his grip, so it goes within him

explanation.surface: A prophetic poet has a firm grip on where websites live.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted phrase goes in after the seer's first letter, not in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonneteer writes sonnets, fourteen-line poems, so is a kind of poet.

clue.text: Doctrine unaffected by revolution?

indicators.note: turned end to end, the word comes out exactly the same

explanation.surface: A belief so firm that no uprising could shake it.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolution suggests politics; here it means turning the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle held as true by a church or school of thought.

clue.text: Mixed drink prior to winning fight

blocks.note: up = ahead, as in two goals up

explanation.surface: A bowl of punch gets drunk just before a brawl breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Mixed looks like an anagram signal, but it only describes the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A punch-up is British slang for a brawl with fists.

clue.text: Coax salesman over petition to limit publicity

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned over means the word is read upwards

blocks.note: to sue is to petition a court

explanation.surface: A salesman gets round a petition that would restrict advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: Over reads as 'about' in the surface; in a down clue it flips the salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to win someone round gently, by talk rather than force.

clue.text: Jog, say, with horse heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling north means reading from the bottom up

blocks.note: a dun is a greyish-brown horse

explanation.surface: A rider jogs along on a horse pointing north.
explanation.walkthrough: Jog looks like running, but here it is the verb for a little push.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone's elbow is to give it a light push, as a reminder.

clue.text: Colour lines somewhat regular

explanation.surface: Coloured lines on a page look fairly regular.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines looks like a noun; it is the verb, and regular is a noun too.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitué is someone who frequents a place, like a regular at a pub.

clue.text: Point legal duty out — one may do so in court

definitions.text: one may do so in court

indicators.note: the letters are put out of their order, as a bone is put out of joint

explanation.surface: A defendant points out that he had no legal duty, as one might in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom surface makes the whole clue read as legal argument, so the answer sits naturally in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant answering a charge at trial enters a plea, and denying it is one plea open to them.

clue.text: Kelly, in films, gets a lot of credit dealing with make-up

indicators.note: most of the word but not all of it, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: Gene Kelly, star of Singin' in the Rain
TICK = credit, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A film star earns plenty on account from his work in the make-up department.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying on tick is old British slang for buying on credit. Make-up here is genetic make-up, not cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetic concerns genes, the inherited code that sets a creature's biological constitution.

clue.text: Rising mist round delta area by the River Don

indicators.note: in a down clue, a rising word is read upwards
the rest is set beside it, following on

blocks.note: D is delta in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Fog lifts from a delta near a river called the Don.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Don is a real river in Yorkshire, which disguises Don as a Mafia boss.
explanation.definitionFit: In Mafia usage a don is a boss, and The Godfather made that title famous.

clue.text: Nearly ignoring nobleman recalling sight seen on safari?

blocks.note: à la = in the style of, so recalling

explanation.surface: A traveller almost overlooks an aristocrat while reminiscing about a safari.
explanation.walkthrough: Nearly looks like 'almost'; it is the word to be emptied of the nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned southern African antelope, one of the animals tourists hope to spot.

clue.text: Swallow vermouth, dishonest over drink? Don’t object

blocks.note: It is Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Someone knocks back vermouth and lies about their drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' just stacks one piece above the next. The definition is an imperative.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something lying down is to accept an insult meekly, without protest.

clue.text: Caught heron hiding head in wooden box with strings

indicators.note: the bird's first letter is hidden away, so it drops out

blocks.note: BITTERN, a heron, without its B

explanation.surface: A heron is trapped in a crate strung with netting.
explanation.walkthrough: The bittern is a kind of heron. The box with strings is a musical instrument, not a cage.
explanation.definitionFit: The cittern is a Renaissance plucked instrument: a wooden body strung with wire.

clue.text: Eating around 6, party first in restaurant sent back staff to find water

explanation.surface: A restaurant party sends its food back to the staff and asks for water.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff means a stick, not waiters, and the 6 refers to nothing in the grid: it is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowsers walk with a forked stick that is said to dip over underground water.

clue.text: Place for rolls of cash head of bank takes out

explanation.surface: A bank manager withdraws rolls of banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rolls of cash suggests banknotes; the rolls are bread rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread rolls are served at the table in a small basket.

clue.text: Match about to occupy a long time

explanation.surface: A sports fixture looks set to drag on for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Match is the verb, as two witness accounts match, not a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that match correspond with each other in every detail.

clue.text: Under most stress, and kind of cross before ordeal

explanation.surface: Someone at breaking point and angry ahead of a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross looks like an adjective for angry; it is the noun, a T-shaped cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope pulled tight carries tension; the tautest one bears the greatest strain.

clue.text: Embroider an accessory worn by son after little drink

blocks.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits
a tie is a neck accessory

explanation.surface: A boy sews an accessory after a quick nip of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Embroider means to exaggerate a story here, not needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroider a tale is to add colourful invented detail, making it more theatrical.

clue.text: Player who, to resolve a pay dispute, made the issue vanish?

definitions.text: Player who, to resolve a pay dispute, made the issue vanish?

blocks.clueFragment: Player who, to resolve a pay dispute,
blocks.note: the player is a musician, cheated of his fee by a town
issue = offspring; the town's children disappear

explanation.surface: A negotiator settles a wage row by making the problem disappear.
explanation.walkthrough: Player means a musician; issue means children. Unpaid for ridding the town of rats, the piper led its children away.
explanation.definitionFit: In the legend the piper, refused his fee after luring away the rats, piped the town's children into a mountain.

clue.text: One books trio playing religious music

explanation.surface: Someone hires a three-piece band to perform church music.
explanation.walkthrough: Books is the verb 'hires' on the surface; in the wordplay it is a set of scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: An introit is the psalm or chant sung as the priest approaches the altar at Mass.

clue.text: Official not losing heart after mean answer

indicators.note: the heart is the middle, so the central letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A petty official stays upbeat despite a stingy reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Mean looks like stingy; it is a verb. 'Not losing heart' reads as encouragement, but is an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: An intendant was a royal administrator in old France or Spain, running a province.

clue.text: Like some lodges with family members in charge

blocks.note: a mother and a son, two members of a family

explanation.surface: Holiday lodges run by a family.
explanation.walkthrough: Lodges suggests holiday cabins; here it means a branch of a society.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons meet in local branches called lodges, so those lodges are Masonic.

clue.text: Return strange material for jewellery

blocks.note: to return an MP is to elect them

explanation.surface: A jeweller sends back some odd stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Return looks like a reversal signal but is the election sense. Strange looks like an anagram signal but is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrum is a natural alloy of gold and silver, worked into ancient ornaments and coins.

clue.text: Periodically scratched, plain carpet is free

indicators.note: letters are struck out at regular intervals, every other one

blocks.note: p(L)a(I)n with alternate letters struck out
to carpet someone is to scold them

explanation.surface: A plain carpet, scratched at intervals, is going for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Carpet is the verb: being carpeted is being told off by the boss. Free is a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate prisoners is to release them from captivity.

clue.text: What creates atmosphere in stadium: header for Man United saved by defender thus

indicators.note: a header is what comes at the top

blocks.note: a back is a defender in football
standard abbreviation, as in team names

explanation.surface: A football report: a header from a Manchester United player is kept out by a defender.
explanation.walkthrough: The football vocabulary is all wordplay; the definition is the soundtrack in a film or a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiet music played under a scene or in a restaurant sets the mood without being listened to.

clue.text: Is it wrong to oust leaders in firm?

indicators.note: the leaders are the first letters, and each one is thrown out

explanation.surface: A question about ethics: may a board depose the bosses of a company?
explanation.walkthrough: Firm looks like a company, and leaders look like its bosses. Firm is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm grip or structure is solid and hard to shift.

clue.text: Solo number coming up — do badly with notes

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from the bottom
the letters are arranged badly, out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A soloist's number comes round and they fluff the notes.
explanation.walkthrough: Do and notes read as a botched performance; together they are the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: On one's tod is British rhyming slang (Tod Sloan, own) for on one's own, alone.

clue.text: Make invalid discern changes

indicators.note: the letters are changed round into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to spot the changes that void a document.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as spot-the-difference; changes is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescind a law or contract is to revoke it so it no longer has force.

clue.text: Alter tune – dare to get a remix

indicators.note: a remix rearranges existing material, so the letters are mixed again

explanation.surface: A DJ changes a track, bold enough to put out a remix.
explanation.walkthrough: Alter tune looks like a single instruction; Alter is the definition by itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To denature a substance is to change its essential properties, as heat does to proteins.

clue.text: After a couple of litres, that man’s in public dance in a state

indicators.note: the rest of the wordplay follows these opening letters

explanation.surface: A man who has had two litres is dancing in public in quite a state.
explanation.walkthrough: In a state means in a mess, not in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: All over the shop is British slang for chaotic and disorganised, which being in a state also means.

clue.text: Accountants beside old tree

explanation.surface: Accountants stand next to an ancient tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural gives two chartered accountants.
explanation.definitionFit: The cacao is the tropical evergreen whose beans are made into cocoa and chocolate.

clue.text: Time off work for Otto I, hosting king with great natural resources

blocks.note: TOIL = work, minus T for time
ich is German for I, as a German emperor would say it

explanation.surface: A German emperor takes leave from ruling and entertains another king.
explanation.walkthrough: Time off work reads as a holiday; it is an instruction. Otto I was a tenth-century German king and emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: A country with plentiful petroleum reserves is well endowed with a valuable natural resource.

clue.text: From Virginia, book somewhere to stay in Florida

explanation.surface: Book a hotel in Florida, travelling from Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: Virginia looks like the US state; it is the novelist Virginia Woolf.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolf's gender-shifting novel shares its title with the Florida city of theme parks and hotels.

clue.text: The writer’s letter has no information — it may provoke a defensive reaction

definitions.text: it may provoke a defensive reaction

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: The author's letter is empty of news and may get a prickly response.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer's means 'the writer is', not 'my'. The defensive reaction is the body's, not the reader's.
explanation.definitionFit: An immunogen is a substance that triggers the body's immune system into responding.

clue.text: Battle knight — try to follow horse

blocks.note: a mare is a female horse
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight in battle tries to keep up with his horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Marengo was also the name of Napoleon's own horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon defeated the Austrians at Marengo in northern Italy in 1800.

clue.text: Doctor loves catching European opera

blocks.note: love = O, zero in tennis; two of them

explanation.surface: A doctor loves meeting a European at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor is the verb to falsify, not a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is Verdi's 1851 work about a court jester, a staple of the operatic repertoire.

clue.text: One helping criminal venture featured in 18 letters?

blocks.note: the first 18 letters of the alphabet run A to R
to bet is to venture a stake

explanation.surface: An accomplice's scheme turns up in the answer to 18 across.
explanation.walkthrough: The 18 looks like a cross-reference to the Pied Piper; it counts letters of the alphabet instead.
explanation.definitionFit: An abettor encourages or assists someone in committing a crime, as in 'aiding and abetting'.

clue.text: Punch yobbo roughly to start with

blocks.note: yobbo is British slang for a lout

explanation.surface: A thug lashes out and hits someone first.
explanation.walkthrough: Roughly looks like it describes the yobbo, but gives the abbreviation for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A clout is a heavy blow with the hand, the same as a punch.

clue.text: Making fast run beset by sound of farm animals

explanation.surface: A runner hurries past lowing cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast means secure here, as a boat is made fast, not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooring a boat means tying it securely to a buoy or quay.

clue.text: Type of rock with gold and jade around Welsh area

blocks.note: a jade is a worn-out horse, a nag

explanation.surface: A geologist finds rock with gold and jade stone in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock and jade look geological; one is music and the other an old horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamorgan is a historic county of south Wales, home to Cardiff and Swansea.

clue.text: Car in front of Escort, say

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
the first letter goes in ahead of the rest of the answer

explanation.surface: A Ford Escort parked ahead of another car.
explanation.walkthrough: The Escort is a Ford model, which pulls the eye to car types. Say is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: British English calls a station wagon an estate car, or simply an estate.

clue.text: Somewhere sailors may be, smuggling ecstasy and crack

indicators.note: the drug is carried hidden inside, as contraband is smuggled

explanation.surface: Sailors are caught smuggling ecstasy and crack cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: Crack reads as the drug alongside ecstasy; it is a quip.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a witty remark, and a one-liner is a joke delivered in a single sentence.

clue.text: Large, unnerving character showing caution

explanation.surface: A big, unsettling figure acting warily.
explanation.walkthrough: Character looks like a person; it means a quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Being leery of something means being wary and suspicious of it.

clue.text: Eating tonnes occasionally, like French soup

indicators.note: only now and then, so every other letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone eating tonnes now and then, as the French like their soup.
explanation.walkthrough: Like French reads as fondness for French food; it is a translation instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a clear, clarified broth served as a starter.

clue.text: Child holding new suit strangely ends cartoon film

indicators.note: the letters are set out strangely

explanation.surface: A child in a new outfit oddly ends up watching a cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Cartoon points at animation, but the film is live action. Suit is cards, not clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind Hearts and Coronets is a 1949 Ealing Studios black comedy starring Alec Guinness.

clue.text: Maybe one’s bowled over family doctor with case of indigestion

blocks.note: first and last letters of indigestion

explanation.surface: Someone is overwhelmed by the family doctor treating their indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowled over reads as amazed; it is literal, as a skittle is knocked down.
explanation.definitionFit: In skittles and tenpin bowling, the kingpin is a key target knocked flat by the ball.

clue.text: Job secured by potentially stout supporter

blocks.note: stout is a kind of ale, so ale is potentially stout

explanation.surface: A job landed by a portly backer.
explanation.walkthrough: Stout reads as fat; it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a passionate advocate of a cause, as in an apostle of free trade.

clue.text: Bondage deforms elastic

indicators.note: elastic material stretches into new shapes, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: Being tied up leaves the elastic bent out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Elastic sits at the end like a noun, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval serfs were bound to their lord's land and could not leave it.

clue.text: Smoke swirling over new elementary particle

explanation.surface: Smoke swirls above a newly found particle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' just places the smoke above the new letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The K-meson, or kaon, is a subatomic particle made of a quark and an antiquark.

clue.text: Feeling less energy after playing hit song

blocks.note: a record that is on is playing

explanation.surface: A performer feels flat after singing their hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word is numb-er, more numb, not a song number.
explanation.definitionFit: A record that tops the charts is at number one, the biggest hit of its week.

clue.text: English team upset the Spanish one away from home

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means tipped over

blocks.note: a team of eleven, as in cricket or football

explanation.surface: An English side is beaten by Spain's in an away match.
explanation.walkthrough: Away from home looks like a football fixture; it is someone banished.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile has been banished from, or forced to leave, their native country.

clue.text: Fought in ring, asked to absorb pressure

blocks.note: to pose a question is to ask it

explanation.surface: A boxer who fought in the ring was asked to soak up pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Fought in ring reads as boxing, but the ring is only a letter shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose a plan is to resist it and campaign against it.

clue.text: Vow to turn up dressed in secretary’s platforms

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from the bottom

explanation.surface: A secretary turns up in platform shoes to take her vows.
explanation.walkthrough: Platforms suggests shoes; these are raised stages.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is a raised stand for a speaker or conductor; the Latin plural takes -a.

clue.text: Star turn keeping finale of routine up

indicators.note: a finale is the closing part, so take the last letter
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom

explanation.surface: The headline act saves the best of the routine for the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Star turn reads as a headline act; the star is the definition and turn is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Deneb is the brightest point of light in Cygnus, the swan constellation.

clue.text: Targeting property of popular American rock band

explanation.surface: A popular American rock band with a knack for acquiring real estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Property sounds like real estate; the definition is a legal term.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action in rem (Latin, 'against a thing') is brought against an item rather than a person.

clue.text: Court winner being successful in attempt

blocks.note: passing an exam is being successful

explanation.surface: A lawyer wins a court case by succeeding at the attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: Court suggests law; it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, a winner is an unreturnable ball, and a passing shot beats an opponent rushing the net.

clue.text: Vague insinuations heard — they get harder to hear

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken, so the phrase is said aloud to give the answer

explanation.surface: Rumours that are muttered grow fainter as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits after the dash and reads as a comment on the rumours.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, passages marked for a gradual decrease in volume grow steadily quieter.

clue.text: London university splitting gas particle

explanation.surface: A London university lab splits a gas particle.
explanation.walkthrough: Splitting suggests splitting the atom; it only means going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleon is a proton or neutron, one of the constituents of an atomic nucleus.

clue.text: Arrive earlier than partner, gutted by online assignation?

indicators.note: a gutted fish has its insides removed, leaving just the outer letters

blocks.note: an e-date, a date arranged online

explanation.surface: A partner turns up early and is gutted by a date they set up online.
explanation.walkthrough: Gutted reads as upset; it means emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: To predate something is to come before it in time, existing or happening first.

clue.text: Flamboyant winger and token supporter of match

blocks.note: George Best, the Manchester United winger
a man is a playing piece in draughts or chess

explanation.surface: A showy football winger and a token substitute back the team in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Match looks like a football game; it is a marriage. George Best was a famous Northern Irish footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: At a wedding the groom's chief attendant stands beside him and hands over the rings.
